heroHeadline: Kast Signs Santiago Commitment With Four Neighbors Against Organized Crime as Nation Braces for First Cuenta Pública on June 1
heroSubtitle: President José Antonio Kast hosted a five-nation security summit on May 28 — signing the 'Santiago Commitment' intelligence-sharing pact with Argentina, Peru, Ecuador, and Bolivia to confront transnational organized crime. The summit followed Chile's fastest post-dictatorship cabinet reshuffle (May 19): Security Minister Trinidad Steinert and spokesperson Mara Sedini were removed amid falling approval. The Kast government's flagship economic reactivation bill — cutting corporate taxes from 27% to 23% — cleared the Chamber 90-59-1 and now faces Senate scrutiny over the contested 25-year tax stability clause. COCHILCO raised its 2026 copper price forecast to US$5.55/lb as LME spot hit a record US$6.39/lb, brightening Chile's fiscal outlook even as Q1 GDP contracted 0.5%. The Mapuche werkén Huenchullán case continues in Collipulli with prosecutors seeking 18 years. Kast's approval sits at 26-39% ahead of his first June 1 address to Congress.
footerNote: Data sourced from official Chilean government records (Biblioteca del Congreso, Banco Central, SERVEL), Rettig and Valech commissions, IACHR, CIPER Chile, and major international outlets.
